This is a preview release. Existing installations are not offered it as an update.

### New

- **The merge points at the right display.** Some displays report a different identifier
  once you change display mode, which reads as a different display. The settings page used
  to list every shared display that was not on screen and leave the choice to you; for
  models known to do this, it now preselects the right one and says "Known to be another
  display mode of …". Merging still happens only when you confirm it, and nothing is
  preselected when more than one display could be meant.
- **`muxsu-cli list --json`.** Prints the displays this host enumerates in a
  machine-readable form. The existing text output is unchanged.

### Fixes

- **"About MuxSU" named the upstream author as the developer.** The row read Henry Hsu,
  who wrote the original DisplayMux; the licence has always kept the two apart. It now
  names MuxSU's own author, and the upstream credit stays in the note below the list.
- **One display counted as two across hosts.** An EDID holds two unrelated serial numbers —
  a text descriptor and a 32-bit number — and Windows reads the text one while macOS reads
  the number, so one display can report two entirely different serials. The development
  tool that compares identities read that as two separate displays; it now only compares
  serials read from the same field. Switching in the app is unaffected: that case was
  always covered by matching on the model.

### Also

- `product-facts.md` now records the two-serial-field behaviour above, with tests so it
  cannot be quietly undone later.

This release uses the same protocol as v0.7.1 (`5`), so the two pair and switch with each
other.

### Known limitations

- The table behind the merge suggestion currently holds one model confirmed on real
  hardware: the MSI MPG 274U's `MSI:3CF0` and `MSI:7CF0`. Every other display behaves as
  before — the merge is still offered, just without a preselection.
- The backend half of this feature has unit tests but has not yet been taken through a real
  display-mode change on hardware end to end. That is what this preview is for.
- A switch from the tray that fails shows no message; it is logged, and reported if
  diagnostics are allowed.
- The macOS DMG uses an ad-hoc signature and is not notarized with an Apple Developer ID,
  so Gatekeeper may ask you to allow it manually.
